title: Add jj-integration test suite and fix path-restricted commit bugs
description:
A class of bugs leaks pebbles state into the working copy instead of into commits. Caught in the wild in computer_management: a 2026-05-01 title rename of bug af8bb1ad left `D bug-...-current-rel.json` and `M index.json` uncommitted for ~3 days, hidden under unrelated descendant commits.

## Root cause

`JJ::commit()` (src/jj.rs:68-89) runs `jj commit -m "<msg>" <single-file-path>`. jj's path-restricted commit only includes changes touching those paths, so any other paths the same operation modified remain in the working copy.

`Operations` callers always pass *one* path — the new/current issue file — even when the operation also:
- modifies `.pebbles/index.json` (every create / delete / rename), and/or
- deletes the old issue file (every rename).

## Per-operation analysis

What actually changes on disk vs. what gets committed today:

| Op | Files changed on disk | Currently committed | Bug? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `init` | index.json | index.json | ok |
| `new` | new issue file, index.json | new issue file | misses index.json |
| `status` | issue file (no index churn) | issue file | ok |
| `update --description` | issue file | issue file | ok |
| `update --title` (rename) | new file, old file (deletion), index.json | new file | misses old file + index.json ← original bug |
| `update --title --description` | same as rename | new file | same |
| `link` (add_relationship) | source issue file | source issue file | ok |
| `unlink` (remove_relationship) | source issue file | source issue file | ok |
| `convert` (rename) | new file, old file (deletion), index.json | new file | misses old file + index.json |
| `delete` | issue file (deletion), index.json | issue file (deletion) | misses index.json |

So `new`, `delete`, `update --title`, and `convert` all leak `index.json` modifications; the two rename ops additionally leak the old-file deletion.

## Test approach

A new `tests/jj_integration.rs` integration test suite. Pebbles is a binary-only crate; tests drive the binary as a subprocess via `std::process::Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_pebbles"))` (no new lib.rs, no extra dependency for the binary lookup; `tempfile` added as a dev-dep for tempdirs).

Each test:

1. Creates a tempdir via tempfile::TempDir (rooted under $TMPDIR — outside any other repo).
2. Sets PEBBLES_DB_PATH=<tmp>/.pebbles. Does NOT create a .no_jj marker.
3. Runs a sequence of mutating pebbles subcommands.
4. After each operation, asserts the three invariants below.

Issue filenames are not predicted via Issue::file_name (would require lib-ifying the crate). Instead the test reads the on-disk `.pebbles/index.json` after each command to learn what filename pebbles chose, and records old filenames *before* a rename so deletions can be asserted against the actual paths pebbles used. This also keeps the test honest end-to-end: it exercises the same code path users hit.

## Per-step invariants

After every successful pebbles operation:

1. **Working copy clean.** `jj diff --summary` produces no output. Catches "operation left changes uncommitted."
2. **No paths outside .pebbles/.** All paths affected by any commit since test start are under .pebbles/. Catches "pebbles slurped up unrelated user changes." Check at end of sequence over `root()..@-`.
3. **HEAD commit affected-path set matches expectation.** The set of paths changed in @- equals the expected set for the operation just performed.

Implementation note for invariant 3: jj reports renames as `R {old => new}` (single line, two paths) when content is similar enough, falling back to `A new` + `D old` when content differs substantially. Verified empirically: renames with small content changes (e.g., one extra line) still report as R; only wholesale replacement falls back to A+D. The test must therefore predicate on *affected path sets* parsed from --summary lines (where R contributes both paths), not on literal line counts. SPEC.md:223 currently asserts "jj tracks this as a delete + add (not a rename)" as if it were unconditional — this is wrong as a general statement and should be corrected as part of this work.

## Test matrix

Each test starts from `pebbles init` in a fresh tempdir.

| # | Sequence | Expected affected paths in last commit |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | init | {index.json} |
| T2 | init → new "Foo" bug | {new file, index.json} |
| T3 | T2 → status in_progress | {issue file} |
| T4 | T2 → update --description | {issue file} |
| T5 | T2 → update --title "Bar" | {new file, old file, index.json} |
| T6 | T2 → new "Other" → link required_for | {source issue file} |
| T7 | T6 → unlink | {source issue file} |
| T8 | T2 → convert usecase | {new file, old file, index.json} |
| T9 | T2 → delete | {issue file, index.json} |

(For renames in T5/T8, "affected paths" means the union of A/D/R-from/R-to/M paths; whether jj reports R vs A+D is implementation-dependent and not asserted.)

## Implementation plan (red-green TDD)

1. Write tests/jj_integration.rs with all 9 tests using current (buggy) binary. Run; T2, T5, T8, T9 should fail on invariant 3 (and possibly invariant 1, depending on order of assertions); T1, T3, T4, T6, T7 should pass.
2. Fix the bugs:
   - Change JJ::commit to accept a slice of paths, pass all of them to `jj commit`.
   - In Storage::save_issue, return the set of changed paths (new file path; optionally old file path on rename) so callers know what to commit.
   - In Operations callers (create, update, delete, convert), pass the full set including index.json (and old issue file on rename) to jj.commit.
3. Re-run tests. All 9 should pass.
4. Update SPEC.md §"File Renaming" / §"Jujutsu Integration" to reflect: every commit includes index.json when the index changed, includes the old file path when the issue was renamed, and jj may render a rename as R or as D+A depending on content similarity.

## Out of scope

- Mocking jj behind a trait (TESTABILITY_ANALYSIS.md proposal). This suite needs *real* jj precisely because it's verifying the integration. Mocking would defeat the purpose.
- Testing failed-operation behavior (relationship validation errors, ambiguous IDs, etc.) — should leave no commit and no working-copy changes. Worth a follow-up pebble; not v1 of this suite.
- Idempotent operations (e.g., setting the same status twice). Behavior is currently to bump updated_at and commit anyway; pinning that is a separate concern.
- The independent leakage symptom where running `pebbles` while cwd is inside this repo's own tests/ fixtures produces stray commits in pebbles' git history. Same root cause (path-restricted commit doesn't isolate the caller from the repo) but a different fix shape (refuse to operate inside an unrelated repo, or scope to the .pebbles/ subdir). Track separately.
